chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the one who is compelled to eat the dead animal (beast of burden) while he finds game (to eat). He said: He should eat the game. I said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has permitted him the dead animal if he is compelled to it, and has not permitted him the game. He said: Which is more beloved to you, to eat from your wealth or the dead animal? I said: I will eat from my wealth. He said: It is your wealth because the ransom is upon you. I said: If there is no wealth with me? He said: You will pay it off when you return to your wealth.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: Dead animal (specifically a beast of burden like a camel or cow in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred option for someone forced to eat a dead animal if they can also eat halal game?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of necessity (darura) by distinguishing between the permissibility of consuming game and the preferential obligation to consume the dead animal while incurring a financial liability (fidah). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that preserving one's wealth through a debt is often preferred over consuming permissible food, reflecting a nuanced balance between physical survival and economic responsibility. The dialogue highlights the practical application of 'necessity permits the prohibited' while maintaining the sanctity of lawful sustenance.
